Opus files play, and Ond now tells you when a new version is out.

### Downloads

| File | For |
| --- | --- |
| `Ond-0.4.2-macos-universal.dmg` (or `.zip`) | macOS 11 or later, Apple silicon and Intel |
| `Ond-0.4.2-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | Linux on x86_64, glibc 2.39 or newer (Ubuntu 24.04, Fedora 40, Debian 13) |
| `Ond-0.4.2-linux-aarch64.tar.gz` | Linux on ARM64, same requirements |
| `Ond-0.4.2-windows-x86_64.zip` | Windows 10 and 11. Still untested on real hardware; issues welcome. |

On NixOS or with Nix: `nix profile install github:Solidsilver/ond/v0.4.2`. Install steps for every platform are in the [README](https://github.com/Solidsilver/ond#install).

### Opus

- `.opus` files play. They didn't before because the decoder Ond uses has no Opus support. Ond now includes libopus. Opus files can also be analyzed for loudness and waveforms.

### Update notices

- Once a day, Ond checks GitHub for a newer release. When there is one, a notice above the sidebar's footer links to its release notes and download. You can also skip that version.
- Turn it off in Settings › General › Check for updates. Settings also shows the version you have.
- Copies installed with Nix don't check, because Nix updates them.
- This is the first release that checks, so the first notice you'll see is for the release after this one.

### Smaller changes

- The README's macOS steps cover macOS 15, where right-click › Open no longer opens an unsigned app.
- Dependency updates.
